chapter: New York years and Manhattan School
title: Session work for Ernie Wilkins and buying a house in Teaneck
summary: Record sessions through Ernie Wilkins, including the Ray Brown album 1st Bassman, let him buy a Teaneck home.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Such as getting into the recording. Ernie, you know Ernie Wilkins?

He was giving me a lot of uh record sessions, when I, I finally got enough money to, to purchase a home in Teaneck, New Jersey, because of Mingus and Ernie Wilkins. And during that we period recorded 1st Bassman. Ernie Wilkins wrote the music for uh the bassist um...Ray Brown.
Yeah. I remember that session. Cannonball was in the saxophone section. Earle Warren was playing first alto.
Cannonball, third [alto]. Budd Johnson was playing the other tenor...
...and I was playing one. That was a grand feeling playing with those musicians.
